mutateSurfaceSplit.excludedRangesNote: the two ISO code data lines (ISO 4217 alpha-3 list and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 list, 1-indexed lines 65-68 inclusive) at the time of this entry; run-mutation-tier re-verifies the pinned sha256 of exactly these lines on every run and hard-fails on drift.
mutateSurfaceSplit.reason: Inline reference data, not kernel behaviour: the ISO 4217 alpha-3 and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 membership sets are unmodified standard code lists inlined as data because compute() must stay a self-contained pure function for the zkVM guest (no imports, no side files). Mutating a published code list string is not the kernel-authoring floor: membership behaviour at the leaf-walk level is scored (a non-member country code refusal and member-code acceptance are covered by fixtures, reachability vectors and proptest properties), and the kernel own arithmetic (roll-forward, sums, tolerance, HHI, readiness, thresholds) stays fully scored. Same data-exclusion pattern as art-780 vendored bundle and rca-01 fdlibm.
